title: SSC CHSL Tier-2 — Mock Test 4
description: Full-length 100-question mock simulating the latest SSC CGL Tier-1 pattern. 60 minutes total, no sectional timing, 2 marks/Q, -0.5 negative. Includes 5 inline Current-Affairs questions in the GA section (T20 World Cup 2026, Bhubaneswar 2028, PMGSY-III extension, AI Impact Summit, BioAsia 2026) — refreshable from the admin CA pool.

questions.stem: If the letters of the word 'EQUATION' are arranged in alphabetical order, which letter occupies the FOURTH position from the left?
questions.explanation: Letters of EQUATION sorted alphabetically: A, E, I, N, O, Q, T, U. The 4th letter is N.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Find the missing term: AZ, CX, EV, GT, ?
questions.explanation: First letters: A(+2)→C(+2)→E(+2)→G(+2)→I. Second letters: Z(−2)→X(−2)→V(−2)→T(−2)→R. Next term: IR.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Find the missing term: 2, 5, 11, 23, 47, ?
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Find the next term: 4, 9, 19, 39, 79, ?
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: In a certain code, 'WATER' is written as 'XBUFS'. How is 'JUICE' written?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts +1: W→X, A→B, T→U, E→F, R→S. Apply to JUICE: J→K, U→V, I→J, C→D, E→F → KVJDF.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If 'TIGER' is coded as 20-9-7-5-18, how is 'LION' coded?
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Pointing to a photograph, Sita said, 'She is the only daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is the girl in the photograph related to Sita?
questions.explanation: Sita's grandfather's only son = Sita's father. The only daughter of Sita's father = Sita herself.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If A is the brother of B, B is the sister of C, and C is the father of D, how is A related to D?
questions.explanation: C is D's father. B is C's sister, so B is D's aunt. A is B's brother, so A is D's uncle.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Anand walks 8 km North, then turns right and walks 6 km, then turns right and walks 12 km, then turns right and walks 6 km. How far is he from the starting point and in which direction?
questions.explanation: N 8 → E 6 → S 12 → W 6. Net N-S: 8 − 12 = −4 (i.e. 4 km South). Net E-W: 6 − 6 = 0. So 4 km South.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Sunil walks 3 km East, turns left and walks 4 km North. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: 3-4-5 right triangle: distance = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 km.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All flowers are plants. Some plants are trees.

Conclusions:
I. Some flowers are trees.
II. All trees are plants.
questions.explanation: I: All flowers ⊂ Plants; some plants are trees — flowers and trees may not overlap. NOT necessarily true. II: 'Some plants are trees' does NOT mean ALL trees are plants. NOT necessarily true. Neither follows.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All cats are mammals. All mammals are warm-blooded.

Conclusions:
I. All cats are warm-blooded.
II. Some warm-blooded are cats.
questions.explanation: I: Cats ⊂ Mammals ⊂ Warm-blooded ⟹ Cats ⊂ Warm-blooded. TRUE. II: From I, all cats are warm-blooded, so some warm-blooded are cats. TRUE. Both follow.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statement: The Government has decided to ban the use of plastic bags from January 2027.

Course of Action:
I. Manufacturers should be informed in advance.
II. Eco-friendly alternatives must be made available.
questions.explanation: Both actions are necessary follow-ups to a plastic ban — give manufacturers transition time AND ensure alternatives. Both follow.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If A > B = C, and C > D ≥ E, which of the following is DEFINITELY TRUE?
questions.explanation: A > B = C > D ≥ E. So A > C > D ≥ E ⟹ A > E. TRUE.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Five friends — P, Q, R, S, T — sit in a row facing North. R is at one end. T is to the immediate right of R. Q is to the immediate right of T. S is between Q and P. Who is at the other end?
questions.explanation: Order from left: R, T, Q, S, P. R is at the left end. P is at the right end.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If 1 January 2024 was a Monday, what day of the week was 1 January 2025?
questions.explanation: 2024 is a leap year (366 days). 366 mod 7 = 2 odd days. Monday + 2 = Wednesday.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand at 3:30?
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: A cube of side 4 cm is painted on all faces and then cut into smaller cubes of side 1 cm. How many small cubes have NO painted face?
questions.explanation: A cube divided into n³ = 4³ = 64 small cubes. Cubes with no painted face = (n−2)³ = 2³ = 8.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: How many triangles are there in the figure formed by joining the four corners of a square with both diagonals AND a horizontal line through the centre?
questions.explanation: The diagonals + horizontal create 4 small triangles + 4 medium triangles = 8 triangles.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.explanation: 49=7², 121=11², 144=12² — all perfect squares. 150 is not. So 150 is odd.

questions.stem: DOCTOR : STETHOSCOPE :: CARPENTER : ?
questions.explanation: Stethoscope is the primary diagnostic tool of a doctor. Saw is the primary cutting tool of a carpenter (more characteristic than a hammer for cutting/shaping wood).
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Question: How is P related to Q?

Statement I: P is the brother of R, who is the wife of Q.
Statement II: Q has only one brother-in-law.
questions.explanation: From I: P is R's brother; R is Q's wife ⟹ P is Q's brother-in-law. SUFFICIENT. II alone tells us Q has 1 brother-in-law but not who. So I alone.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If '+' means '×' and '−' means '+', what is the value of:  8 + 4 − 6 + 2
questions.explanation: Substitute: '+'→'×', '−'→'+'. Expression becomes 8 × 4 + 6 × 2. By BODMAS: 8×4 = 32; 6×2 = 12. Sum = 32 + 12 = 44.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Which constitutional body is responsible for conducting elections to the offices of the President and Vice-President of India?
questions.explanation: Article 324 vests the superintendence and conduct of elections (including President & VP) in the Election Commission of India.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can the President proclaim Financial Emergency?
questions.explanation: Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency. (Article 352 = National Emergency; Article 356 = President's Rule.)
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The Lokpal of India is appointed by the President on the recommendation of a selection committee. Who chairs this committee?
questions.explanation: The Lokpal selection committee is chaired by the Prime Minister and includes the Speaker, Leader of Opposition, CJI (or his nominee), and an eminent jurist.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: In Indian Parliament, the 'Zero Hour' refers to:
options: The first hour of the parliamentary session
The hour when no business is conducted
The hour starting at 12 noon when MPs raise issues without prior notice
questions.explanation: Zero Hour starts at 12 noon (after Question Hour) and lasts until the lunch break. MPs can raise matters of urgent public importance without prior notice.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to states and UTs?
questions.explanation: The Fourth Schedule allocates Rajya Sabha seats to each state and UT.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The Permanent Settlement of Bengal in 1793 was introduced by which Governor-General?
questions.explanation: Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement (Zamindari System) in Bengal in 1793, fixing land revenue permanently.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The 'Doctrine of Lapse' associated with Lord Dalhousie was first applied to which Indian state?
questions.explanation: The Doctrine of Lapse was first applied to Satara in 1848. Other annexations followed: Jaitpur, Sambhalpur, Jhansi, Nagpur.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Who founded the 'Servants of India Society' in 1905 to dedicate Indians to public service?
questions.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society on 12 June 1905 in Pune.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has India's longest coastline at approximately 1,600 km, followed by Andhra Pradesh (~975 km).
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The Tropic of Cancer passes through which of the following Indian states?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N) passes through 8 Indian states including Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: The Sundarbans Mangrove forest is located in the delta of which river system?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans is the world's largest mangrove forest, formed in the delta of the Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers.
questions.subject: GENERAL_AWARENESS

questions.stem: Which vitamin's deficiency causes the disease 'Beri-Beri'?
questions.explanation: Beri-Beri is caused by Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) deficiency, affecting the nervous system.

questions.stem: The chemical formula of Plaster of Paris is:
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris (POP) is calcium sulphate hemihydrate: CaSO₄·½H₂O.

questions.stem: The unit of electric resistance is:
questions.explanation: Resistance is measured in Ohms (Ω). Voltage in volts, current in amperes, power in watts.

questions.stem: Which gas is most abundant in the Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Earth's atmosphere is approximately 78% Nitrogen, 21% Oxygen, 1% Argon and other gases.

questions.stem: In which year was the National Mission for Clean Ganga (Namami Gange) launched?
questions.explanation: Namami Gange Programme was launched in June 2014 as an integrated mission for Ganga rejuvenation.

questions.stem: Which is India's highest peace-time gallantry award?
questions.explanation: Ashok Chakra is the highest peace-time gallantry award. Param Vir Chakra is the highest WAR-time award.

questions.stem: Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu, traditionally performed in temples of Tamil Nadu.

questions.stem: Who composed the National Song 'Vande Mataram'?
questions.explanation: 'Vande Mataram' was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in 1875 and later included in his novel 'Anandamath' (1882).

questions.stem: Which is the largest river basin in India by area?
questions.explanation: The Ganga Basin covers ~26% of India's land area (~1.08 million sq km) — the largest river basin in India.

questions.stem: BioAsia 2026, India's flagship international life-sciences conference, was held in which city in February 2026?

questions.stem: The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 360. If one of the numbers is 60, find the other.
questions.explanation: HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers ⟹ 12 × 360 = 60 × x ⟹ x = 4320/60 = 72.

questions.stem: If the price of petrol increases by 25%, by what percentage must consumption be reduced to keep the expenditure unchanged?
questions.explanation: Required reduction% = (increase / (100 + increase)) × 100 = (25/125) × 100 = 20%.

questions.stem: In a mixture of milk and water, the ratio is 5:3. If 8 litres of water is added, the ratio becomes 5:5. Find the original quantity of milk.
questions.explanation: Let milk = 5x, water = 3x. After adding 8 L water: 5x:(3x+8) = 5:5 = 1:1 ⟹ 5x = 3x + 8 ⟹ x = 4. Milk = 5(4) = 20 L.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: Divide ₹2,800 among A, B, C in the ratio 2:3:5.

questions.stem: A and B together can finish a piece of work in 12 days. A alone can do it in 18 days. In how many days can B alone do it?

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours, Pipe B in 8 hours. If both are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/6 + 1/8 = (4+3)/24 = 7/24 per hour. Time = 24/7 ≈ 3.4286 hours = 3 h 25.7 min ≈ 3 h 26 min.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: A train 200 m long crosses a platform 100 m long in 12 seconds. Find the speed of the train in km/h.
questions.explanation: Distance = 200 + 100 = 300 m in 12 s. Speed = 25 m/s = 25 × 18/5 = 90 km/h.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: A boat covers 24 km downstream in 3 hours and the same distance upstream in 4 hours. Find the speed of the stream.
questions.explanation: Downstream = 24/3 = 8; Upstream = 24/4 = 6. Stream speed = (8 − 6)/2 = 1 km/h.
questions.subject: QUANT

questions.stem: The average of 7 consecutive odd numbers is 21. Find the smallest of these numbers.
questions.explanation: Middle = 21 (4th term). 7 consecutive odd numbers: 15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 25, 27. Smallest = 15.

questions.stem: The average age of 30 students is 12 years. If the teacher's age is included, the average becomes 13. Find the teacher's age.
questions.explanation: Sum of students = 30 × 12 = 360. Sum with teacher = 31 × 13 = 403. Teacher = 403 − 360 = 43.

questions.stem: Which of the following best captures the author's view on AI in healthcare?
questions.passage_context: Artificial intelligence is increasingly being deployed in healthcare, with applications ranging from diagnostic imaging to drug discovery. Proponents argue that AI can analyse vast quantities of medical data far more rapidly than any human, identifying subtle patterns that might escape even experienced clinicians. Critics, however, warn of three principal risks: opaque decision-making (the so-called 'black box' problem), data bias arising from unrepresentative training sets, and over-reliance on technology that may erode clinical judgement. Regulators in most major economies are now drafting frameworks that require explainability, equitable performance across demographic groups, and clear accountability when AI-assisted decisions fail. The likely outcome is not a wholesale replacement of doctors but a careful integration in which AI augments rather than substitutes human expertise.
options: AI will fully replace doctors soon
AI should not be used in healthcare at all
AI should augment, not replace, human clinical expertise
AI's risks make it unfit for any healthcare role
questions.explanation: The closing line: 'a careful integration in which AI augments rather than substitutes human expertise.'
questions.subject: ENGLISH

(A) Neither the principal / (B) nor the teachers / (C) was present / (D) at the meeting.

questions.stem:
Choose the correct passive form:

'The chef is preparing the meal.'
options: The meal is being prepared by the chef.
The meal was prepared by the chef.
The meal has been prepared by the chef.
The meal will be prepared by the chef.
questions.explanation: Present continuous active 'is V-ing' becomes present continuous passive 'is being V3'.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Choose the correct passive form:

'They will announce the results tomorrow.'
options: The results will be announced tomorrow.
The results have been announced tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Future simple active 'will V' becomes future simple passive 'will be V3'.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Rearrange and identify the FIRST sentence.

(A) The result has been a sharp decline in air quality.
(B) Cities across South Asia have witnessed alarming pollution levels in recent years.
(C) Stubble burning, vehicular emissions, and industrial output all contribute.
(D) Governments have begun to invest in monitoring and mitigation infrastructure.
(E) However, enforcement remains inconsistent.
questions.explanation: B (intro: pollution problem) → C (causes) → A (result) → D (govt response) → E (limit). 1st = B.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Rearrange and identify the LAST sentence.

(A) Mathematics is often considered an abstract discipline.
(B) Yet it underpins almost every modern technology, from smartphones to spacecraft.
(C) Without strong mathematical foundations, scientific progress would be severely limited.
(D) This is why investment in mathematics education remains a national priority.
(E) Encouraging young students to pursue maths is essential for the country's future.
questions.explanation: A (intro) → B (qualifier) → C (consequence) → D (policy implication) → E (call to action). Last = E.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:

She _has been working_ here since 2018.
questions.explanation: 'Since 2018' (point in time) requires the present-perfect-continuous: 'has been working'.

questions.stem: Convert to indirect speech: She said, 'I will go tomorrow.'

She said that she will go tomorrow.
